 1   §25.192. Transmission Service Rates.

 2   (a)   Applicability. This section applies to all transmission service providers (TSPs) providing

 3         transmission service within the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) region, to

 4         all distribution service providers (DSPs) serving load within the ERCOT region, to all

 5         entities scheduling the export of power out of the ERCOT region, and to other transmission

 6         service customers in of the ERCOT region. transmission system.

 7

 8   (b)   Definitions. The following terms, when used in this section, have the following meanings,

 9         unless context indicates otherwise.

10         (1)    Baseline values -- Values that reflect the costs or other information used to

11                establish rates in a rate proceeding.

12         (2)    Behind-the-meter load -- Load served at a site where all or a portion of the load’s

13                electricity consumption is supplied by an on-site generation resource or energy

14                storage resource that is authorized to take service from the ERCOT system.

15         (3)    Direct interconnection costs -- All costs associated with the facilities required to

16                physically interconnect or upgrade the interconnection of a load, or a distinct set of

17                loads, to the existing ERCOT system, including interconnection lines, substation

18                additions or modifications, and associated equipment necessary to establish or

19                modify service.

20         (4)    DSP 12 coincident peak (12CP) demand value load -- The average of the 12

21                demand values of a DSP that are coincident with the ERCOT 12CP intervals

22                determined from the total demand of all customers within the ERCOT region

23                connected to a DSP, including load served at transmission voltage, behind-the-
  1          meter load, and , wholesale storage load, and block load transfers, but excluding

 2          the portion of demand attributable to the export of power out of the ERCOT region.

 3          flows.

 4   (5)(3) DSP billing demand -- The transmission billing demand associated with

 5          distribution service providers, as determined by the DSP 12CP demand value and

 6          the adjustment to the DSP 12CP demand value under subsection (f) of this section.

 7   (6)    ERCOT 12CP demand value load -- The sum of the DSP 12CP load demand

 8          value for all the DSPs serving load in the ERCOT region, including wholesale

 9          storage load and block load transfers, but excluding the portion of demand

10          attributable to the export of power out of the ERCOT region. flows.

11   (7)(4) ERCOT 12CP intervals -- The set of 12 30-minute intervals in which the highest

12          ERCOT system demand occurs each month, as measured over each 30-minute

13          period that starts at the beginning of each hour and at each 15-minute increment

14          thereafter, composed of the ERCOT system monthly peak demand interval for each

15          of the 12 calendar months from October 1 of one year through September 30 of the

16          subsequent year, inclusive.

17   (8)(5) ERCOT System -- ERCOT system as that term is defined in ERCOT protocols.

18          Export entity -- An ERCOT-registered entity scheduling the export of power from

19          the ERCOT region, including a qualified scheduling entity.

20   (9)(6) Large load customer -- An entity that must comply with is subject to §25.194 of

21          this title (relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards), regardless of whether

22          it is new, expanded, or behind-the-meter load.
  1   (10)(7) Large load minimum billing demand -- The minimum transmission billing

 2          demand associated with large load customers, as described by §25.193 of this title

 3          (relating to Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factor

 4          (TCRF)).

 5   (11)(8) Network export rate -- The transmission rate established by the commission for a

 6          TSP to recover the costs associated with the use of that TSP’s transmission facilities

 7          to provide wholesale transmission service at transmission voltage for the delivery

 8          of power to be exported from the ERCOT region.

 9   (12)(9) Network transmission service rate -- The transmission rate established by the

10          commission for a TSP to recover costs associated with the use of that TSP’s

11          transmission facilities to provide wholesale transmission service at transmission

12          voltage within the ERCOT region.

13   (13)(10)      Non-investor-owned utility distribution service provider (non-IOU

14          DSP) -- A DSP that is a municipally owned utility, river authority, or electric

15          cooperative.

16   (14)(11)      Non-investor-owned utility transmission service provider (non-IOU

17          TSP) -- A TSP that is a municipally owned utility, river authority, or electric

18          cooperative.

19   (15)(12)      Settlement quality meter data -- Settlement quality meter data as that term

20          is defined in ERCOT protocols.

21   (16)   System upgrades -- Facilities required to improve the reliability of the ERCOT

22          system, improve the power flow of the ERCOT system, or increase the capacity

23          that can be transported across the ERCOT system, including transmission lines,
  1          substations, and transformers that are not direct interconnection costs. Tie line -- A

 2          facility connected to the ERCOT transmission grid that enables power to be

 3          imported into or exported out of the ERCOT power grid, including high voltage

 4          direct current converter stations and variable frequency transformers.

 5   (13)   Transmission interconnection costs -- All costs associated with the facilities

 6          required to physically interconnect or upgrade the interconnection of a

 7          transmission-level customer, or a distinct set of transmission-level customers, to

 8          the existing transmission network, including interconnection lines, substation

 9          additions or modifications, and associated equipment necessary to establish or

10          modify service.

11   (17)(14)       Wholesale storage load -- Load associated solely and entirely with

12          wholesale storage, as described by §25.501(m)(2) of this title (relating to Wholesale

13          Market Design for the Electric Reliability Council of Texas).

14   (15)   Wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage -- Wholesale

15          transmission service provided using facilities that are rated at less than 60 kilovolts

16          and that are not transmission facilities as described in subsection (e) of this section,

17          as required by §25.191(d)(2) of this title (relating to Transmission Service

18          Requirements).

19   (16)   Wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage rate -- The transmission

20          rate established by the commission for a TSP or DSP to recover costs associated

21          with the use of that utility’s distribution facilities to provide wholesale transmission

22          service at distribution voltage.

  1   (c)   Tariffs.

 2   (1)   Each TSP must file a tariff for transmission service to reflect the rates, terms, and

 3         conditions approved set by the commission and must apply its tariff on a non-

 4         discriminatory basis.

 5         (2)    If the TSP provides wholesale transmission service at distribution voltage, the tariff

 6                required by this section must include a separate section to reflect wholesale

 7                transmission service at distribution voltage rates, terms, and conditions set by the

 8                commission. A TSP must file an application to establish such tariff within 30 days

 9                of receiving a request for such service.

10

11   (d)   Charges for network transmission service delivered within the ERCOT region. DSPs

12         must incur transmission service charges as provided by the tariffs of a TSP.

13         (1)    A TSP’s network transmission service rate must be calculated as its commission-

14                approved transmission cost of service divided by the ERCOT 12CP demand value

15                as adjusted under subsection (f) of this section load. In a proceeding to establish

16                network transmission service rates under this section, the ERCOT 12CP load value

17                to be used in calculating a TSP’s rate must be the most recently approved ERCOT

18                12CP loaddemand value in effect prior to the date of approval of the TSP’s new

19                network transmission service rate in the proceeding. The rate approved may not

20                exceed the noticed rate under any circumstance.

21         (2)    A TSP’s network transmission service rate must remain in effect until the

22                commission approves a new rate and that new rate takes effect. The TSP’s annual

23                rate must be converted to a monthly rate. The monthly network transmission
  1                service charge to be paid by each DSP is the product of each TSP’s monthly rate as

 2                specified in its tariff and the DSP’s previous year’s DSP 12CP loaddemand value.

 3         (3)    Payments for transmission services must be consistent with commission orders,

 4                approved tariffs, and §25.202 of this title (relating to Commercial Terms for

 5                Transmission Service).

 6

 7   (e)   Transmission cost of service. A TSP’s transmission cost of service must be calculated in

 8         accordance with this subsection and the amount approved by the commission will be based

 9         on a complete review of all aspects of a TSP’s transmission cost of service.

10         (1)    The transmission cost of service for each TSP must be based on:

11                (A)     the expenses in Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) expense

12                        accounts 560-573 (or accounts with similar contents or amounts properly

13                        functionalized to the transmission function);

14                (B)     the depreciation, federal income tax, other associated taxes, and the

15                        commission-allowed rate of return associated with FERC plant accounts

16                        350-359 (or accounts with similar contents or amounts properly

17                        functionalized to the transmission function), less accumulated depreciation

18                        and accumulated deferred federal income taxes; and

19                (C)     the offsetting reduction to transmission cost of service for any network

20                        export rate revenues as described in subsection (g)(2) of this section.

21         (2)    Transmission facilities.

22                (A)     Transmission facilities include the following:
  1                (i)     power lines, substations, reactive devices, and associated facilities,

 2                        operated at 60 kilovolts or above, including radial lines operated at

 3                        or above 60 kilovolts, except the step-up transformers and a

 4                        protective device associated with the interconnection from a

 5                        generating station or a storage facility to the transmission network;

 6                (ii)    substation facilities on the high side of the transformer, in a

 7                        substation where power is transformed from a voltage higher than

 8                        60 kilovolts to a voltage lower than 60 kilovolts;

 9                (iii)   the portion of direct current tie-line interconnections with areas

10                        outside of the ERCOT region (DC ties) that are owned by a TSP in

11                        the ERCOT region, including those portions of the DC tie line that

12                        operate at a voltage lower than 60 kilovolts; and

13                (iv)    capacitors and other reactive devices that are operated at a voltage

14                        below 60 kilovolts, if they are located in a distribution substation,

15                        the load at the substation has a power factor in excess of 0.95 as

16                        measured or calculated at the distribution voltage level without the

17                        reactive devices, and the reactive devices are controlled by an

18                        operator or automatically switched in response to transmission

19                        voltage.

20         (B)    As used in subparagraph (A) of this paragraph, reactive devices do not

21                include generating facilities or energy storage facilities.

22   (3)   For municipally owned utilities, river authorities, and electric cooperatives, the

23         commission may permit the use of the cash flow method or other reasonable
  1         alternative methods of determining the annual transmission revenue requirement,

 2         including the return element of the revenue requirement, consistent with the rate

 3         actions of the rate-setting authority for a municipally owned utility. For a non-IOU

 4         TSP, the commission may permit the use of the cash flow method or other

 5         reasonable alternative methods of determining the annual transmission revenue

 6         requirement, including the return element of the revenue requirement, consistent

 7         with the rate actions of the rate-setting authority for a municipally owned utility.

 8   (4)   For municipally owned utilities, river authorities, and electric cooperatives, the

 9         return may be determined based on the TSP’s actual debt service and a reasonable

10         coverage ratio. In determining a reasonable coverage ratio, the commission will

11         consider the coverage ratios required in the TSP’s bond indentures or ordinances

12         and the most recent rate action of the rate setting authority for the TSP. For a non-

13         IOU TSP, the return may be determined based on the non-IOU TSP’s actual debt

14         service and a reasonable debt service coverage ratio or interest coverage ratio. In

15         determining a reasonable coverage ratio, the commission will consider the coverage

16         ratios required in the non-IOUTSP’s bond indentures or ordinances and the most

17         recent rate action of the retail rate-setting authority for the non-IOU TSP, if any.

18   (5)   A municipally owned utility that is required to apply for a certificate of public

19         convenience and necessity to construct, install, or extend a transmission facility

20         within ERCOT under §25.101 of this title (relating to Certification Criteria) is

21         entitled to recover, through its transmission rates under this section, reasonable

22         payments made to a taxing entity in lieu of ad valorem taxes on that transmission

23         facility, provided that:
  1         (A)    The municipally owned utility enters into a written agreement with the

 2                governing body of the taxing entity related to the payments;

 3         (B)    The amount paid is the same as the amount the municipally owned utility

 4                would have to pay to the taxing entity on that transmission facility if the

 5                facility were subject to ad valorem taxation;

 6         (C)    The governing body of the taxing entity is not the governing body of the

 7                municipally owned utility; and

 8         (D)    The municipally owned utility provides the commission with a copy of the

 9                written agreement and any other information that the commission considers

10                necessary in relation to the agreement.

11   (6)   A TSP must not include in the TSP’s transmission cost of service or the TSP’s
12         transmission service rates the direct Notwithstanding any other provision of this
13         section, transmission interconnection costs associated with a standard large load
14         interconnection agreement that is executed under the requirements of §25.194 of
15         this Title (relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards). agreements signed
16         after the effective date of this section must not be included in a TSP’s transmission
17         cost of service or transmission service rates.
18   (7)   With regard to investments for which the commission has approved a certificate of
19         convenience and necessity but which have not been authorized by the commission
20         as used and useful in providing service to the public, and for which investments the
21         associated costs have not yet been approved by the commission as prudently
22         incurred, an application under subsection (d)(1) of this section must include, in the
23         transmission utility rate filing package, a comparison of the cost estimates provided
24         in any certificate of convenience and necessity proceedings with the actual costs
25         incurred for those investments.
26   (8)   Baseline values.      Any network transmission service rate and associated
27         transmission cost of service approved by the commission under this section must
28         establish baseline values that reflect the costs used to establish the transmission
  1                rates. At a minimum, reasonable and accurate baseline values for invested capital,
 2                rate base, return on rate base, capital structure, cost of debt, operations and
 3                maintenance expense, depreciation expense, federal income tax expense, other
 4                taxes expense, depreciation rates, network export-rate revenues, and other revenues
 5                must be established.
 6         (9)    The commission may adopt rate-filing requirements that provide additional details

 7                concerning the costs that may be included in transmission rates and how such costs

 8                should be reported in a proceeding to establish or amend transmission rates.

 9

10   (f)   DSP billing demand. Billing units. The DSP billing demands units determined under

11         this subsection must be used to determine a TSP’s rates established under this section.

12         (1)    DSP 12CP demand value. No later than December 1 of each year, ERCOT must

13                determine and file with the commission the current year’s DSP 12CP demand value

14                load for each DSP in the ERCOT region, based on the ERCOT 12CP intervals

15                during the 12-month period ending on the last day of the immediately preceding

16                September. ERCOT must also include in this filing the ERCOT 12CP load for the

17                current year. The measurement of the ERCOT system monthly peak demand for

18                purposes of determining the ERCOT 12CP intervals and the determination of the

19                DSP demand values that coincide with the ERCOT 12CP intervals must be in

20                accordance with ERCOT protocols. Following notice and an opportunity for a

21                hearing, the The commission may approve changes to DSP 12CP demand values

22                and the ERCOT 12CP demand value at any time.

23                (A)     Non-investor-owned Non-IOU DSPs must provide ERCOT timely access

24                        to settlement-quality meter data for each large load customer that the non-

25                        investor-owned DSP serves within its service territory.
  1         (B)    Access to the settlement-quality meter data must be provided in a manner

 2                that enables ERCOT to independently calculate the adjustments to the DSP

 3                12CP demand value that is required by this subsection.

 4         (C)    A non-investor-owned DSP’s transmission operator or TSP may provide

 5                ERCOT access to the settlement-quality meter data on behalf of the non-

 6                investor-owned DSP.

 7   (2)   Adjustment to DSP 12CP demand value. Notwithstanding the applicability of

 8         §25.193 of this title (relating to Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost

 9         Recovery Factor (TCRF)), ERCOT must adjust perform adjustments to each DSP

10         12CP demand load value, including the DSP 12CP demand value of a non-investor-

11         owned DSP, to reflect a large load minimum billing demand for each large load

12         customer served by that DSP.

13         (A)    Calculation of adjustment. The required adjustment to a DSP 12CP

14                demand value must be calculated as follows:

15                (i)    For each large load customer served by the adding to each measured

16                       DSP 12CP load, for each large load customer of that DSP, the

17                       difference between that customer’s large load minimum billing

18                       demand , as described in §25.193 of this title (relating to

19                       Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factor

20                       (TCRF)), and that customer’s measured 12CP demand consistent

21                       with the most recent ERCOT 12CP intervals must be added to the

22                       DSP 12CP demand value of the DSP that serves that large load

23                       customer. For each large load customer served by the DSP, ERCOT
  1                must use the highest large load minimum billing demand value

 2                identified during the 12-month period used to determine the ERCOT

 3                12CP intervals under this subsection in calculating the adjustment

 4                for each month in that period. load, adjusted for line losses as

 5                appropriate and annualized across the annual period for large load

 6                customers initiating their connection within the period or for large

 7                load customers which have increased their contracted peak demand

 8                or NCP demand within the period.

 9         (ii)   Notwithstanding the applicability of §25.193 of this title (relating to

10                Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factor

11                (TCRF)), the required adjustment to the DSP 12CP demand value

12                of a non-investor-owned DSP must use a proxy large load minimum

13                billing demand, determined by §25.193(d), for each large load

14                customer served by that non-investor-owned DSP.

15   (B)   Commencement of adjustment. For each large load customer, ERCOT

16         must commence the adjustment under this subsection for each MW level of

17         available service upon completion of the facilities or upgrades necessary to

18         deliver capacity to the large load customer, as determined by ERCOT,

19         subparagraph must commence at the level of available service at the time it

20         is available, irrespective of whether the large load customer has energized

21         or is fully using the available capacity.

22   (C)   Discontinuation of adjustment. ERCOT must discontinue an adjustment

23         associated with a large load minimum billing demand under this subsection
  1                20 years from the date of commencement or upon written notice from the

 2                DSP that the large load customer’s SLLIA is terminated, whichever is

 3                earlier.

 4   (3)   Filing requirement. No later than December 1 of each year, ERCOT must file a

 5         report with the commission identifying the DSP billing demand for each DSP in

 6         the ERCOT region using data from the 12-month period ending on the last day of

 7         the immediately preceding September.

 8         (A)    ERCOT must identify the following information in the report:

 9                (i)        the ERCOT 12CP demand value;

10                (ii)       the DSP 12CP demand value for each DSP in the ERCOT region;

11                (iii)      the DSP billing demand for each DSP in the ERCOT region;

12                (iv)       the total number of large load customers served by the DSP, as

13                           applicable; and

14                (v)        the total adjustments made to a DSP 12CP demand value, as

15                           applicable.

16         (B)    For each adjustment made to a DSP 12CP demand value, ERCOT must

17                additionally identify the following information in the report;

18                (i)        the large load minimum billing demand associated with each large

19                           load customer that is served by that DSP;

20                (ii)       the date that the adjustment commenced;

21                (iii)      the anticipated date that the adjustment will be discontinued;

22                (iv)       whether an adjustment is discontinued during the 12-month period

23                           ending on the last day of the immediately preceding September; and
  1                        (v)     the basis for discontinuation of an adjustment, as applicable.

 2          (4)    Data retention.

 3                 (A)    Each DSP in the ERCOT region must retain the data that is needed to

 4                        calculate its DSP billing demand, including the underlying data used to

 5                        determine a large load customer’s large load minimum billing demand or

 6                        proxy large load minimum billing demand, for a minimum of 18 months

 7                        from the date that the data is created.

 8                 (B)    ERCOT protocols may prescribe different data retention requirements to

 9                        ensure ERCOT’s ability to implement this subsection.

11   (g)(2) DC tie Tie-line power flows. ERCOT must file a public report with the commission

12          stating the total amount of energy imported and the total amount of energy exported over

13          each DC tie line for the calendar month. The report must also include the total amount of

14          energy exported from the ERCOT region during the reporting month and each of the

15          preceding 11 calendar months, reported by scheduling entity. Each report must be filed

16          within 45 days of the reporting month.

17

18   (h)(g) Transmission rates for exports from ERCOT. A transmission service charge for exports

19          of power from ERCOT must be assessed to transmission service customers for

20          transmission service within the boundaries of the ERCOT region, in accordance with this

21          section and the ERCOT protocols.

22          (1)    A transmission service customer must be assessed a transmission service charge for

23                 the use of the ERCOT transmission system in exporting power from ERCOT based
  1                    on scheduled exports and the rates established under subsections (e) and (f) of this

 2                    section. The intervals must consist of one hour.

 3            (2)     The hourly transmission rate for exports from ERCOT will be the TSP’s annual

 4                    rate established under subsections (e) and (f) of this section divided by 8760.

 5            (3)     The entity scheduling the export of power over a DC tie is solely responsible to the

 6                    TSP for payment of transmission service charges under this subsection.

 7

 8   (i)(h) Transmission revenue. Revenue from the transmission of electric energy out of the

 9            ERCOT region over the DC ties that is recovered under subsection (g) of this section must

10            be credited to all transmission service customers as a reduction in the transmission cost of

11            service for TSPs that receive the revenue.

12

13   (j)(i)   Revision of transmission rates. Each TSP in the ERCOT region must periodically revise

14            its transmission rates under this section to reflect changes in the cost of providing such

15            services. Any request for a change in transmission rates must comply with the filing

16            requirements established by the commission. The commission may, at any time, require a

17            TSP to file an application to revise its rates.

18

19   (k)(j) Interim update of network rates.

20            (1)     Frequency. Each TSP in the ERCOT region may apply to update its network

21                    transmission service rate and its network export rate on an interim basis not more

22                    than twice per calendar year to reflect changes in its invested capital.
  1   (2)   Costs that may be included. If the TSP elects to update its transmission rates, the

 2         new rates must reflect the addition and retirement of transmission facilities and

 3         include appropriate depreciation, federal income tax and other associated taxes, the

 4         commission-authorized rate of return on such facilities, and any adjustments related

 5         to changes in the transmission-related accumulated deferred federal income tax

 6         balance associated with the updated level of transmission facilities, as well as

 7         changes in loads. If the TSP does not have a commission-authorized rate of return,

 8         an appropriate rate of return must be used. Only transmission facilities that have

 9         been interconnected, energized, and are used and useful for providing utility

10         services may be added in an interim update under this section.

11   (3)   Reconciliation. An interim update of network transmission service rates under this

12         subsection must be subject to reconciliation at the next complete review of the

13         TSP’s transmission cost of service, at which time the commission must review the

14         costs of the interim transmission plant additions to determine if they were

15         reasonable and necessary. Any amounts resulting from an interim update that are

16         found to have been unreasonable or unnecessary, plus the corresponding return and

17         taxes, must be refunded with carrying costs determined as follows: for the time

18         period beginning with the date on which over-recovery is determined to have begun

19         to the effective date of the TSP’s rates set in that complete review of the TSP’s

20         transmission cost of service, carrying costs must be calculated using the same rate

21         of return that was applied to the transmission investments included in the update.

22         For the time period beginning with the effective date of the TSP’s rates set in that

23         complete review of the TSPS’s transmission cost of service, carrying costs must be
  1         calculated using the TSP’s rate of return authorized in that complete review. The

 2         commission may order a compliance proceeding to determine the final amounts of

 3         over-recovery that must be refunded to customers and the form of the refund.

 4   (4)   Consideration of the effect on a TSP’s financial risk and rate of return. For a

 5         TSP that has increased its rates under this subsection, the commission may, in

 6         setting rates in the next complete review of the TSP’s transmission cost of service,

 7         expressly consider the effects of reduced regulatory lag resulting from the interim

 8         updates to the TSP’s rates and the concomitant impact on the TSP’s financial risk

 9         and rate of return.

10   (5)   Commission processing of application.          The commission will process an

11         application filed under paragraph (1) of this subsection in the following manner.

12         (A)    Notice and intervention deadline. The applicant must provide notice of

13                its application to all parties in the applicant’s last complete review of the

14                applicant’s transmission cost of service and all of the distribution service

15                providers listed in the last docket in which the commission set the annual

16                transmission service charges and DSP billing demand for the Electric

17                Reliability Council of Texas. The intervention deadline must be 21 days

18                from the date service of notice is completed.

19         (B)    Sufficiency of application. A motion to find an application materially

20                deficient must be filed no later than 21 days after an application is filed.

21                The motion must specify the nature of the deficiency and the relevant

22                portions of the application, and cite the particular requirement with which

23                the application is alleged not to comply. The applicant’s response to a
  1                       motion to find an application materially deficient must be filed no later than

 2                       five working days after such motion is filed. If within ten working days

 3                       after the deadline for filing a motion to find an application materially

 4                       deficient, the presiding officer has not filed a written order concluding that

 5                       material deficiencies exist in the application, the application is deemed

 6                       sufficient.

 7                (C)    Review of application. A proceeding initiated under paragraph (1) of this

 8                       subsection is eligible for disposition under §22.35(b)(1) of this title (relating

 9                       to Informal Disposition). If the requirements of §22.35 of this title are met,

10                       the presiding officer must issue a notice of approval within 60 days of the

11                       date a materially sufficient application is filed unless good cause exists to

12                       extend this deadline or the presiding officer determines that the proceeding

13                       should be considered by the commission.

14         (6)    Filing schedule. The commission may prescribe a schedule for TSPs to file

15                proceedings to revise the rates for transmission services.

16         (7)    Reporting requirements.        Each TSP must file reports that will permit the

17                commission to monitor its transmission costs and revenues, in accordance with any

18                filing requirements and schedules prescribed by the commission.

20   (l)(k) Rate treatment of a large load customer’s outstanding amounts owed, forfeited

21         financial security, and termination fee. Large load customer interconnection fee and

22         financial security.
  1   (1)   Outstanding amounts owed. In all proceedings to adjust rates under this section,

 2         a TSP must apply any payment, including from the drawing down of financial

 3         security, associated with a large load customer’s outstanding amounts owed

 4         pursuant to §25.194 of this title (relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards)

 5         or pursuant to the large load customer’s standard large load interconnection

 6         agreement as an offset to the corresponding cost or expense. Interconnection fee.

 7         A large load customer must pay the interconnecting TSP an interconnection fee in

 8         accordance with §25.194 (relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards). In

 9         all proceedings to adjust rates under this section, TSPs must apply all

10         interconnection fee amounts received as an offset to the TSP’s transmission revenue

11         requirement.

12   (2)   Forfeited financial security. A TSP that receives a payment, including from the

13         drawing down of financial security, associated with a large load customer’s

14         financial security that is forfeited, pursuant to §25.194 of this title (relating to Large

15         Load Interconnection Standards) or pursuant to the large load customer’s standard

16         large load interconnection agreement, must submit an application to the

17         commission to establish a wholesale transmission service credit rider not later than

18         60 days after receipt of the forfeited financial security. Financial security. In all

19         proceedings to adjust rates under this section, TSPs must apply all financial security

20         amounts forfeited pursuant to §25.194 of this title (relating to Large Load

21         Interconnection Standards) as an offset to the TSP’s transmission revenue
